correctness.rationale: Independent uniform parent choices give the conditional telescoping probabilities \(\prod_{j=1}^r(i_j-j)/(n-j)\); exhaustive and rational checks confirm this exact identity. Each joint probability is bounded by the product of leaf marginals. Fixed-order factorial sums on every compact label window converge to powers of the integral of (1-e^{-f})x, with a uniformly summable exponential majorant. Thus the exact finite Laplace expansions converge to the PPP Laplace functional, implying the whole point-process and fixed-rank Gamma limits. All sizes, boundary conventions and quantifiers are specified; finite checks are not used as infinite proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Knowing \(\Pr(I_{n,i}=1)=(i-1)/(n-1)\) does not determine a point process: dependency must be controlled. originality.rationale: The complete joint oldest-leaf label point process and its early-label rare-event factorial intensities are not established in the specifically compared statements. Kuba-Panholzer proves one-label degree laws; Janson describes global leaf-count asymptotics; fixed-root subtree leaf counts and Poisson approximations of unrelated tree statistics do not imply the present process without a new joint rare-event analysis. Previously recorded related leaf-count results concern other observables. Hidden older coverage remains a risk.

value.rationale: The oldest surviving leaves form a natural extremal observable in a model with asymptotically n/2 total leaves. The theorem identifies its nontrivial square-root survival scale, provides all fixed-rank joint order statistics and a structural rare-event Poisson process, while preserving the exact weak finite-size dependence.
